reproduced_defects.title: APPLY.md's documented revert command reverts nothing
reproduced_defects.label: DIRECTLY_REPRODUCED
reproduced_defects.observed: `git checkout <SHA> -- .cursor .gitignore` exits 1 with "error: pathspec '.gitignore' did not match any file(s) known to git", because .gitignore does not exist at the revert SHA — the apply step is what creates it. git checkout with a pathspec is atomic, so it aborts before touching anything: run against the applied tree, .cursor still held 15 files where the base has 1, and .gitignore was still present.
reproduced_defects.second_defect_in_the_same_command: Even with a valid pathspec, `git checkout <SHA> -- .cursor` restores only paths present in that tree. The twelve added files are not in it, so they would survive the revert.
reproduced_defects.third_defect_nearby: APPLY.md's optional backup calls `date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ` twice, once to name the directory and once to name the copy target. If the two calls straddle a second boundary the copy target does not exist, and the failure is swallowed by `2>/dev/null || true`, leaving an empty backup directory that looks like a backup.

reproduced_defects.title: APPLY.md's hook-firing probe is unsafe by construction
reproduced_defects.label: DIRECTLY_REPRODUCED
reproduced_defects.observed: APPLY.md instructs `git push origin main` to prove the guard refuses it. Hook firing was measured in this runtime as NOT firing. Had that instruction been followed here, nothing would have intercepted the command and it would have attempted a push to main — a protected branch under this lane's hard boundaries and under write-scope.json itself.
reproduced_defects.why_it_matters: A probe for a safety net must not be the thing the net was installed to catch. The failing branch of the test is the branch that causes the harm.
reproduced_defects.mechanism_supplied: .cursor/hooks/probe_hook_firing.py, which establishes a control, uses the guard's own audit log as an allow-path witness, and offers only inert deny-path commands. Run --arm, run the printed commands, run --check.

reproduced_defects.title: write-scope.json declares protected_path_globs and nothing reads it
reproduced_defects.label: DIRECTLY_REPRODUCED
reproduced_defects.observed: A repository-wide search for the identifier returns exactly one hit, its own definition in write-scope.json. guard_write_scope.py inspects the command string and the branch, never the staged paths.
reproduced_defects.why_it_matters: It is a key that looks like a boundary and refuses nothing — the same shape as F6, a lesson recorded without a mechanism, inside the very file whose purpose is to be the single enforced statement of scope. A reader checking whether .cursor/** or state/** is protected would conclude yes.
reproduced_defects.action_taken: Labelled advisory and unenforced in place, with the reasoning, rather than deleted or enforced.
reproduced_defects.why_not_enforced: Enforcing it would refuse commits touching .cursor/** and state/**, which are exactly the paths configuration and control-plane lanes legitimately write — including this lane. An over-broad guard blocking legitimate work is the first risk APPLY.md names.
reproduced_defects.why_not_deleted: It records which surfaces a reviewer should look at, which is worth keeping as long as it is not mistaken for protection.

reproduced_defects.title: The repository environment.json is not this environment's configuration source
reproduced_defects.label: DIRECTLY_REPRODUCED observation with a DOCUMENTED tool contract
reproduced_defects.observed: environment-info reports environmentJsonPath: null and source: Team. trigger-environment-build's contract states the environmentJson override 'is not supported for repo-file managed environments (see environmentJsonPath in environment-info) and is rejected for them'. This environment accepted the override and built successfully.
reproduced_defects.conclusion: This environment is db-managed, not repo-file managed. Committing .cursor/environment.json therefore does not by itself change what this estate's agents run.
reproduced_defects.settles: The first open item in L1's could_not_verify table — whether the saved Team environment record is empty or holds config the repository file loses to. It is db-backed, and the repository file is not read as its source.
reproduced_defects.consequence: The applied environment.json is correct, schema-valid and proven to work when the platform is handed its content, and it is inert until the environment record itself is changed. That is a founder action, specified in W2-FOUNDER-ACTIONS.
